clue.text: Cowboy's an argumentative type

blocks.note: first meaning: a ranch hand who herds horses or cattle
second meaning: someone who quarrels or disputes noisily

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome cowboy, picking fights out on the range.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In American ranching a horse handler is so called, while in older English the same word means a person who quarrels or debates.

clue.text: Dreadful wides get note in cricket book

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
N is short for note, as in banknote abbreviations

explanation.surface: A bowler's dreadful wides earn a mention in the cricket record book.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach in cricket. WISDEN is the famous yearly almanack of cricket records.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual Wisden Cricketers' Almanack is the best-known published reference volume for the sport.

clue.text: An Indian quickly going round hotel

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps about another

blocks.note: the article as a single letter
at pace means quickly
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Native American hurrying around a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people of the south-western United States, so a member is an American Indian.

clue.text: Georgia lake has mineral in abundance

blocks.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
L is the map abbreviation for lake
ore is rock from which minerals are mined

explanation.surface: A lake in Georgia is rich in mineral deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word follows a noun to mean plentiful or in large quantities, as in 'prizes galore'.

clue.text: A giant seal on the loose in English region

indicators.note: an escaped animal roams freely, so the letters run wild out of order

blocks.note: all ten letters used

explanation.surface: A huge seal has escaped and is roaming the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the bulge of eastern England covering Norfolk and Suffolk, with a long coastline where seals do live.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of eastern England comprising Norfolk, Suffolk and parts of Cambridgeshire is a recognised geographical area of the country.

clue.text: He's happy, being first to surpass Roger Bannister?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
Bannister ran the first four-minute mile in 1954

explanation.surface: A runner is delighted at being the first to beat Bannister's record.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Bannister as an example of a middle-distance runner, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy person grins a lot, so is someone who grins, a cheerful face-maker.

clue.text: Homer apt to produce a figure of speech

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: all eight letters used

explanation.surface: The poet Homer is well able to turn a fine phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something as another thing it resembles is a classic rhetorical device used in poetry and prose.

clue.text: Labour radical starts to organise in Canada

definitions.note: a place in Canada: the clue names where it is rather than what it is

indicators.note: the starts of several words are their beginnings, so only opening letters of each are kept

blocks.note: the opening three letters, also a common short form of the party
the opening three letters
the opening two letters

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist begins organising in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' applies to all three words, each giving its opening letters. Labrador is the mainland part of the province of Newfoundland and Labrador.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is a large region on the eastern mainland of Canada, so the place is found there.

clue.text: Solitary eccentric is supporter of the monarchy

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are set in an unusual order

blocks.note: all eight letters used

explanation.surface: A lonely oddball turns out to be a devoted fan of the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who backs kings and queens as a system of government is called by this name.

clue.text: Most skimpy underwear involves eroticism first time

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece goes inside another
the first of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: smalls is British slang for underclothes
the opening letter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The skimpiest lingerie brings eroticism for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain smalls are underwear; E sits inside before the final S, then T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment that is most skimpy is the tiniest, the least in size of all.

clue.text: Finally gets fat and squat

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter
tubby means plump

explanation.surface: Someone at last becomes fat and short.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and thick in shape, like a stumpy thumb, is what both words describe.

clue.text: Work here later? It's unreal

indicators.note: as a verb, to work material is to knead and reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
the word as printed less its final R, which the parse has no use for: the setter's slip

explanation.surface: Planning to put in some work here later? That's a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder as printed has a spare R: 'here late' would give the answer exactly, so the setter slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so delicate or otherworldly it seems not of this world can fairly be called unreal.

clue.text: Fancy wraps left in lounge

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Elegant shawls left lying about in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to sit or lie lazily with limbs spread out, the same as to sprawl on a sofa.

clue.text: Tycoon from Berlin, perhaps, is German

blocks.note: Berlin is an example of a capital city
the German word for 'is'

explanation.surface: A wealthy businessman from Berlin turns out to be German.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a rich business magnate, an archetypal owner of wealth invested for profit.

clue.text: Dinosaurs' droppings found in ruins of Sidon

definitions.note: the clue's possessive is surface only; the answer is the plain plural

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so one piece sits within another
ruins are what is left of a wrecked building, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: guano is bird or bat excrement
the ancient Phoenician city, taken as written

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig up dinosaur dung among the ruins of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged city name is split, with the droppings placed after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous period, one of the first ever identified.

clue.text: Selecting commercial alternative

blocks.note: a commercial is an advertisement
an option is an alternative

explanation.surface: Choosing an alternative advertising approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the act of taking up or choosing, as when a policy is adopted; the gerund fits loosely as a noun.

clue.text: He suggests setting Prospero adrift

indicators.note: a boat cast adrift wanders off course, so the letters drift out of order

blocks.note: the magician of The Tempest, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone proposes casting Prospero adrift, as happened to him before The Tempest begins.
explanation.definitionFit: One who puts forward a motion or idea for consideration is the person who makes suggestions.

clue.text: A game girl

blocks.note: first meaning: a card game played alone
second meaning: a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sporting, willing young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A game girl' reads as a plucky woman; split it into two meanings. Patience is the British name for the card game Americans call solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-player card game is called patience in Britain, and it is also a traditional female first name.

clue.text: Sam tried it out for itchy skin

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or inaccurate, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: all ten letters used

explanation.surface: Sam tested a remedy for his itchy rash.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical condition is inflammation of the skin, typically red, sore and irritating.

clue.text: Robin's friend and servant

blocks.note: first meaning: the caped crusader, partner of Robin
second meaning: an army officer's personal attendant

explanation.surface: Robin's companion who also serves him.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British army a batman is an officer's orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book superhero fights crime alongside Robin, and the military term names an officer's personal servant.

clue.text: Croat revolutionary shelters nationalist guerilla

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the letters are turned upside down into new order
to shelter something is to keep it inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: A Croatian rebel hides a nationalist fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Contras were the US-backed rebel fighters in Nicaragua in the 1980s, so a member is an irregular soldier.

clue.text: Cross some lengthy bridges

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the answer is a stretch taken from within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary of the two words

explanation.surface: We cross some long bridges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb but is the noun, a mixture of two breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: In breeding, a cross is the offspring of two different varieties or species, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Philip and Peg produce an apple

blocks.note: Pip is a pet form of Philip, as with the hero of Great Expectations
a peg and a pin both fasten things

explanation.surface: Philip and Peg grow an apple together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a woman's name beside Philip, but it is a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Pippin is a name for several varieties of dessert eating fruit, such as the Cox's Orange Pippin.

clue.text: Liberal Ava is close to Conservative John

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Liberal woman called Ava is intimate with a Conservative man named John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' seems a man's name; in American slang a john is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: John is informal, chiefly American, slang for a toilet or washroom.

clue.text: Anne is crazy lunatic

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all six letters used

explanation.surface: Anne is a raving madwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' and 'lunatic' look like one description; only the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, lunatic means mad or wildly foolish, the same as mentally deranged.

clue.text: Rock Hudson, for example, takes pictures of sailor

blocks.note: to film is to shoot pictures
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: Rock Hudson photographs a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock Hudson was a leading Hollywood actor of the 1950s and 60s, an example of a famous movie celebrity.

clue.text: Took care of sister, perhaps, and daughter

blocks.note: in Britain a sister is a senior nurse
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone looked after a sister and a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' reads as a sibling; in British hospitals it is a senior nurse's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to look after them while ill, so the past tense means looked after.

clue.text: Dad rants about grade

indicators.note: about can mean around or every which way, so the letters are moved round into a new order

blocks.note: all eight letters used

explanation.surface: Father complains loudly about a school mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a level of quality, and a standard is likewise a level against which things are measured.
